title: Actions and Business Logic
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of Actions and Business Logic in a Vue 3 application.
Apply at least one of the syllabus subtopics in a small, inspectable example.
Verify one expected behavior and identify a relevant edge case.

content.intro: This lesson studies Actions and Business Logic within State Management with Pinia. The source PDF subtopics are preserved below and connected to an original working-style example.
content.why_it_matters: Shared state needs a clear source of truth so multiple routes do not drift or duplicate the same business logic.

content_blocks.title: Actions and Business Logic: Shared application state
content_blocks.alt_text: Shared application state diagram for lesson 93: Actions and Business Logic. Read or invoke a relevant store action → Update one source of truth → Use getters or computed data across views
content_blocks.caption: State flow: actions update explicit shared state and derived values keep different views consistent.

content_blocks.title: The idea in context
content_blocks.text: Pinia organizes shared application state into stores with state, getters, and actions; Vuex remains useful legacy knowledge. This lesson focuses on Actions and Business Logic. Start by naming the state, component, browser behavior, or deployment boundary involved; then predict what should change and test the smallest example.

items.title: Synchronous actions
items.text: For Synchronous actions, define one source of truth and separate stored state from derived values and actions. Avoid duplicating the same fact in component-local state and a global store; persist only what the product genuinely needs.

items.title: Asynchronous actions
items.text: For Asynchronous actions, model pending, success, empty, and failure states. Check HTTP status before treating a response as success, cancel stale work where appropriate, and do not let a late response overwrite newer user intent.

items.title: Calling API services from stores
items.text: For Calling API services from stores, define one source of truth and separate stored state from derived values and actions. Avoid duplicating the same fact in component-local state and a global store; persist only what the product genuinely needs.

items.title: Loading and error states
items.text: For Loading and error states, connect the term to a visible behavior in a small Vue 3 example. State what input or reactive dependency changes, predict the UI result, and verify the prediction with a normal case plus a boundary case.

items.title: Organizing actions by responsibility
items.text: For Organizing actions by responsibility, define one source of truth and separate stored state from derived values and actions. Avoid duplicating the same fact in component-local state and a global store; persist only what the product genuinely needs.

content_blocks.expected_output: The store exposes one shared item list, a derived remaining count, and an action to add an item.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Create the store in a JavaScript module, install Pinia with app.use(createPinia()), then call useTasksStore() in setup.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the initial values or original code, reload the development app/test, and repeat once with a boundary or failure case. Remove temporary logs and test data before committing.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Work through Actions and Business Logic with a predict–change–verify loop. First state the expected UI or console output. Change only the relevant input/state value, then observe the result. Compare it with the expected output in the code block; if it differs, check the exact file, runtime/version, browser Console, and network response before widening the investigation.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Extend the example to include “Asynchronous actions”. Keep the same behavior for the ordinary input, then try an empty, invalid, repeated, or failure condition that makes sense for the example. Record the expected result before testing.

items.title: Assuming behavior instead of checking it
items.text: Write down the expected result and reproduce the issue in the smallest possible example; inspect the browser Console and the exact reactive value or request.

items.title: Ignoring an edge case
items.text: Try empty input, a missing item, repeated interaction, a failed request, or unmounting while work is pending; handle the case explicitly.

items.title: Putting every responsibility in one component
items.text: Separate display, reusable logic, API service, and shared state when that boundary makes the behavior easier to test and explain.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: Remember: Pinia organizes shared application state into stores with state, getters, and actions; Vuex remains useful legacy knowledge. For Actions and Business Logic, keep the example small, verify the rendered or logged result, and consult the official references when behavior depends on a specific Vue or ecosystem version.

content_blocks.title: Accessibility, version, and runtime notes
content_blocks.text: Use semantic HTML, readable labels, keyboard-operable controls, and visible errors where the example interacts with users. Vue examples are intended for Vue 3.x with create-vue/Vite unless a legacy or specialist lesson explicitly says otherwise. This CodeLeaf playground does not execute arbitrary Vue code; the snippets are labeled for static validation and should be run in a separate local project.

content.task: Create a small example for “Actions and Business Logic” that applies “Synchronous actions”, predicts the expected result, and verifies a relevant boundary case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates the named Vue concept rather than only mentioning it.
The expected output or observable behavior is written down and can be checked locally.
At least one boundary, loading, invalid-input, or failure case is tested or explicitly reasoned about.
The example uses semantic/accessible interaction patterns and does not treat frontend state as authoritative security.
hints: Start with the smallest observable part of “Synchronous actions”.
Predict the output before changing one input at a time.
Use the browser Console, Vue DevTools, or the appropriate test runner to isolate a mismatch.

common_mistakes.problem: The example only covers the happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Real interfaces receive empty values, delayed responses, invalid input, and failed requests.
common_mistakes.fix: Add one realistic edge/failure case and state its expected behavior.

common_mistakes.problem: The code assumes an API or feature exists in every runtime.
common_mistakes.why: Tool and API support depends on Vue, the build tool, or the chosen SSR/test framework.
common_mistakes.fix: Check the linked official reference and record the runtime/version assumption.

summary: Actions and Business Logic belongs to the broader area State Management with Pinia.
The main concept to practice is Synchronous actions.
Verify a normal result and one meaningful boundary case before using the pattern in a production feature.
